column2: diameter of the wound E2 whose coefficients the card uses (D'Addario Pro Arte Composites hard tension, EJ46C, as measured by Woodhouse 2004). No EJ46C gauge was retrieved: the maker's page refused (HTTP 429), the Wayback request for its old product page returned 404, Strings Direct refused (429), and Salao Musical's listing contradicts itself (.044 in its header, .036 in its table). The card carries the EJ46 E2 radius 0.559 mm (Anderson and Beausoleil 2024) as a declared stand-in
column3: [0.559, 0.6096] mm radius (.044 to .048 in gauge), both ends rendered: partial frequencies identical (beta 1.906e-5, f0 82.361 Hz at both); the 0.6096 mm end decays 0.04 to 0.21 dB/s faster on partials 1 to 24, 1 to 2 percent of the 6.5 to 14.5 dB/s at partials 16 to 24
column4: the string's air drag only: the diameter is the cylinder radius of its per-mode air drag, which the friction and bending factors add to; it does not move the partial frequencies
column5: owner list: D'Addario's EJ46C gauge chart read in a browser, or a micrometer on an EJ46C E2

column2: the loss Woodhouse 2004's eta_A carries beyond the render's computed air drag. His eq. (8) has an air term eta_A/omega with eta_A = 1.2 s^-1; his page calls its form and origin open to question and the fit ad hoc. It is not the computed drag: 2.7 to 12 times larger on partials 1 to 24, so no single diameter reproduces it (7.8 mm radius would at partial 1, 1.6 mm at partial 24)
column3: 3.2 to 3.4 dB/s on partials 17 to 24, mean 3.3 dB/s: the render decays at 6.7 to 14.5 dB/s against 10.0 to 17.7 dB/s for eq. (8) string-only
column4: E2's decay above partial 16 by this amount; it is on no card and is not added to any. It does not account for the grader's decay gap, which reads the first six partials
column5: owner list: a measurement of the same string's air loss in a known gas, or a first-principles account of what eta_A fits; never a fitted term on the card
